short: Benchmark (M03) confirms earlier reports that LaBraM gains nothing on speech EEG; decoders (M06) sit far below same-corpus results; test-subject early stopping (M12).
position: The paper [@khanday2026eegfm] fine-tunes the public LaBraM-Base and EEGMamba checkpoints against CNN baselines on UGR-MINDVOICE and BCIC2020-T3 (M03, M06). M03 is standard: earlier work found LaBraM below EEGNet on silent-speech EEG [@zhou2025lblm] and, on BCIC2020-T3, near 25% balanced accuracy within subject with a linear head and chance across subjects [@wang2025neurottt], so the claim of a first benchmark does not hold. The conclusion that general-purpose EEG pretraining does not transfer rests on two checkpoints; CBraMod reached 0.3976 balanced accuracy with a linear head on the competition's per-subject splits [@wang2025neurottt]. M06 is behind the best comparable work: the best within-subject score, 30.2%, is below deep metric learning's 48.10% on the same corpus [@lee2021dml] and the competition winner's 82.6% [@jeong2022bcicomp]. M12 uses the most frequent leave-one-subject-out design but stops training on the test subject (Sec. 2.4).
